key_insight: UniTB combines physical Hamiltonian priors with equivariant deep learning to generalize across materials chemistry while constraining unphysical electronic states.
engineering_relevance: Its fast UniTB-Flash variant enables large-scale materials screening with linear-cost prior assembly, while UniTB offers more accurate property predictions.
method: Learn E(3)-equivariant corrections to a density-functional tight-binding-inspired Hamiltonian.
Use prior-routed mixture-of-experts learning and a charge-equilibration head.
Bound band shifts through projection; accelerate computation with SO(2) GPU kernels and two-center tables.
evidence_signal: Trained on 29,242 crystals, UniTB achieves 0.48 meV matrix-element error on nonmagnetic test crystals spanning 68 elements; both variants reproduce DFT optics and conductivity for amorphous Ge-Sb-Te without amorphous training data.
watch_item: The reported accuracy covers nonmagnetic crystals, and UniTB-Flash's linear-cost prior assembly does not establish linear scaling for the full electronic-property workflow.
paper_title: Physical structure as an organizing principle for universal Hamiltonian learning
